descriptionAdvanced.en: Puerto Almacén is a historic and vital river port located on the banks of the Ibare River, just 8 kilometers west of the city of Trinidad. It serves as the primary commercial outlet for the capital of Beni, connecting the city with the extensive network of navigable rivers that define the Bolivian Amazon. For generations, this port has been the essential point for the arrival of agricultural products, timber, and livestock from remote river communities. In recent years, Puerto Almacén has also emerged as a significant center for ecotourism, being one of the best locations to observe the rare Pink River Dolphins (Inia boliviensis) in their natural habitat. The port's atmosphere is a vibrant blend of industrious river trade and lush tropical beauty, reflecting the unique water-based culture of the Beni plains.

en: The port is famous for its traditional riverside restaurants that serve fresh fish from the Amazonian rivers.
Puerto Almacén is the gateway to the protected area of the Ibare-Mamoré Municipal Park.
It is a critical logistical node for the transport of cattle between the central savannas and northern processing centers.
The port's name traditionally refers to its role as a massive 'warehouse' (almacén) for regional forest products.
